newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey targets zero budget deficit in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Turkey targets zero budget deficit in 1997.

text.p: Turkey aims for a zero deficit and spending of 6,200 trillion lira in its 1997 draft budget, State Minister Abdullah Gul said on Thursday.
This compares with the revised 1996 deficit target of 1,300 trillion lira and 3,511 trillion in expenditure.
Commenting on the balanced budget, Gul told reporters: "It will...ensure economic stability."

He said 1,600 trillion lira of the 1997 budget spending would be for personnel, 3,300 trillion lira for transfer spendings which mainly consists of interest payments on domestic and foreign borrowings, 500 trillion lira for investments and 668 trillion lira for other areas of expenditure.
The government expected 4,300 trillion lira from tax revenues, Gul said.

Gul said two sets of government measures to raise resources to close public and trade deficits as well as investments through the build-operate-transfer scheme, which stipulates the builder to finance the project, would help realise the zero deficit target next year.
"One aspect of this budget is that it reduces borrowing requirement," he said.
He said average maturity in domestic borrowing was also targeted to be extended to about nine months from the present three to four months.
He did not give other details.
Officials told Reuters non-tax revenues including 422 trillion lira from privatisation and several funds would amount to 1,420 trillion lira next year.
